concept.name: Rule adherence
concept.definition: The degree to which actual trading behavior matches the written rules of the trading plan - entries, exits, sizing, and risk limits taken as specified, with deviations logged. It is the primary process metric of trading discipline.
concept.intuition: The system only works if the operator runs it; rule adherence measures whether you ran your system or your mood.
concept.mechanics: Each trade is scored rule by rule (valid setup, correct size, stop honored, exit per plan); the adherence rate is the share of fully compliant trades. Deviations are classified (early entry, moved stop, oversized, revenge trade) and tracked over time in the journal.
concept.formula: Rule adherence (%) = (number of trades fully compliant with plan rules) / (total trades) x 100.
concept.failure_modes: High adherence to a bad system yields consistent losses - adherence measures fidelity, not edge. Rules written with ambiguity cannot be scored, which makes adherence unmeasurable and review toothless.
concept.misconceptions: Perfect adherence is not rigidity: planned, documented rule changes made in review are part of the process, while improvising mid-trade is not. A winning trade that broke rules counts as an adherence failure, not a success.
concept.example: A trader's month shows 22 of 25 trades fully compliant (88%); the three violations - all moved stops - account for 60% of the month's drawdown.

citations.source: Mike Bellafiore, One Good Trade: Inside the Highly Competitive World of Proprietary Trading (Wiley, 2010) - publisher page
